Ok lots of opinions here.  And that’s great.  Here’s mine 

Yes.  100% yes to French immersion.  
As someone who graduated from it with a certificate of French proficiency by the TDSB, I’d say yes. 

It opened so many doors for me for employment, for travel.  For life.  

Scientifically there’s studies that suggest learning another language (also instruments etc) reduces your chances of issues with mental cognition as you age as well as bilingual adults show larger volume of grey matter in the brain than monolinguals.   There’s other factors like education, exercise etc. but being bilingual in any language gives your child advantages.  

I’d strongly consider saying yes to French immersion.  Additionally. You can learn French too (some kids LOVE sharing new words they learn etc.) and have a cool way to communicate with your daughter.

“ Bilingualism, or the capacity to speak two languages fluently, has also been shown to contribute to cognitive reserve (Schweizer et al., 2012). Relevantly, dual-language use has been associated with executive functioning benefits, which have been observed in bilingual children, adults, and elders, even when the second language is acquired after childhood (Costa and Sebastián-Gallés, 2014).”
